children.name: Lead
children.text: An AI-driven maritime control interface & lever operation optimisation for the next-generation ship bridge — built with Wärtsilä.

children.name: ★ DIA DESIGN INTELLIGENCE AWAR
children.text: ★ DIA DESIGN INTELLIGENCE AWARD · HONORABLE MENTION AND ABOVE

children.name: Value
children.text: Wärtsilä × Aalto Design Factory — Product Development Project (PDP)

children.name: Value
children.text: 7 members, multidisciplinary · Sponsors: Davide Lamparelli, Lauri Tiainen

children.name: Value
children.text: Maritime HMI · AI decision support · Energy efficiency · Alarm management

children.name: Value
children.text: UI/UX design & front-end dev — energy & alarm interfaces, AI interaction logic

children.name: Body
children.text: Aligned with Wärtsilä’s ProTouch system, the project explores how UI/UX design and AI can optimise vessel operation — lowering information load and improving efficiency, safety and human–machine interaction, while supporting low-emission sailing.

children.name: Body
children.text: An AI-driven advisory system built on energy and alarm models, plus a cloud-based smart log connecting the bridge and the engine control room (ECR). A transparent-screen interface and an AI advice agent help the captain and engineers make faster, data-based decisions.

children.name: Desc
children.text: Routes power through ESS to cut consumption

children.name: Desc
children.text: Optimises routing & lever operation in real time

children.name: Desc
children.text: Prioritises and filters warnings through AI

children.name: Lead
children.text: Four modes let the captain match power strategy to voyage conditions. Beneath every mode, the Energy Optimizer routes demand through ESS battery storage, keeping the main engine within its optimal efficiency range.

children.name: Mount · ENERGY DASHBOARD on the bridge

caption.text: ENERGY DASHBOARD on the bridge console — optimizer, ESS battery, energy flow and speed over ground in one view.

children.name: Body
children.text: A vessel monitoring interface for Wärtsilä’s ProTouch system: real-time main-engine status, ESS battery level and energy use across fuel types. The central Energy Index shows power flowing between renewable sources, propulsion and onboard consumers — in Auto-Pilot and manual modes.

children.name: Body
children.text: A side-view pop-up maps the lever, giving a realistic sense of its current position against the optimised one.

children.name: Body
children.text: Continuously routes demand peaks through the ESS battery, keeping the main engine in its optimal efficiency range.

children.name: Lead
children.text: Thrust guidance gives suggestions from real-time data and route-specific conditions, so the operator can make more energy-efficient decisions. A rating system makes the crew’s sustainable performance visible.

children.name: Mount · CO-PILOT NAVIGATION on the bri

caption.text: CO-PILOT NAVIGATION on the bridge console — route corridor, thrust guidance and sustainability index side by side.

children.name: Body
children.text: Combines emission- and fuel-related parameters with timing and smoothing factors into one synthetic analysis.

children.name: Body
children.text: Scores corridor accuracy, speed optimisation, arrival timing, fuel efficiency and operational smoothness — grading each voyage from S to D.

children.name: Body
children.text: Fusing sensor data with AIS, 3D modelling data and historical logs, the lever track shows where the AI would set thrust — the most intuitive way to visualise optimisation.

children.name: Lead
children.text: An intelligent alarm system that groups related alerts, highlights root causes, suggests actions with AI and syncs real-time logs — reducing cognitive load and supporting decisions in complex environments.

children.name: Mount · GROUPED VIEW — grouped alarm l

caption.text: GROUPED VIEW — grouped alarm list on the bridge console, related alerts clustered under their root cause.

children.name: Mount · Engineer’s mobile flow — own r

caption.text: Engineer’s mobile flow — own responsibilities → action options → step details → feedback.
Alarm detail — responsibility assignment, sensor reading and the synced action log.

children.name: b
children.text: AI identifies the root cause across interrelated issues, helping operators focus only on what matters most.

children.name: b
children.text: Combines vessel sensor data and user manuals to suggest actions with confidence scores and clear reasoning, plus step-by-step decision support.

children.name: b
children.text: As engineers follow the steps on their device, the bridge interface shows their actions and feedback in sync.

children.text: Edge-first, advisory-only. How data, models and people connect on board — and how the alarm intelligence groups first, then suggests, and learns from every response.

caption.text: SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE — vessel systems → read-only gateway → Edge AI unit (energy optimizer, navigation co-pilot, alarm grouping GNN, action suggestion RAG + LLM) → bridge console, transparent screen, engineer mobile → captain, officers, engineers. Shore cloud handles fleet history, training and versioned updates.

caption.text: AI IMPLEMENTATION · ALARM INTELLIGENCE — online on the vessel in real time (stream → live alarm graph → grouping & root cause → evidence retrieval → grounded suggestion → UI → engineer response); offline on shore, periodic retraining from fleet history and feedback.

children.name: Lead
children.text: From a first ferry visit to a working bridge-console prototype: nine months with Wärtsilä, tested with the people who would actually use it — Finnlines captains and crew.

children.name: Quote
children.text: We took the prototype to the people who would use it.

caption.text: VISIT 01 · DISCOVERY · AUTUMN 2025 — saw bridge and engine-room work first-hand and talked with the crew about alarms and energy decisions.
VISIT 02 · VALIDATION · SPRING 2026 — put the bridge-console prototype in front of Finnlines captains and crew and collected their feedback.
